title: A Triangulation Test for Possible Thermodynamic Contributions to Gravitational Lensing in Galaxy Clusters
description: Introduces a triangulation methodology that compares lensing mass, hydrostatic mass, and ICM entropy gradients to test for small thermodynamic contributions to gravitational lensing in galaxy clusters. Applies the method to the Bullet Cluster and Abell 1835, finding no significant correlation at current sensitivity and outlining consistency requirements and detection thresholds for future stacked analyses.
author: Morten Magnusson

lensing_mass.description: Projected enclosed mass from gravitational lensing using the mean convergence within radius r.

critical_surface_density.description: Critical surface density that sets the geometric lensing efficiency for a lens at D_l and sources at D_s.

hydrostatic_equilibrium.description: Equation of hydrostatic equilibrium relating pressure gradient to enclosed mass and gas density.

hydrostatic_mass.latex: M_{\rm HSE}(<r) = -\, \frac{k T(r) \, r}{\mu m_{p} G} \left[ \frac{\mathrm{d} \ln n_{e}}{\mathrm{d} \ln r} + \frac{\mathrm{d} \ln T}{\mathrm{d} \ln r} \right]
hydrostatic_mass.description: Enclosed mass inferred from X-ray temperature and density profiles under hydrostatic equilibrium.

mass_residual.description: Residual mass profile used to search for structure not captured by hydrostatic modeling.

entropy.description: ICM entropy proxy proportional to specific entropy for an ideal gas.

entropy_gradient.description: Magnitude of the entropy gradient used as a tracer of ICM thermodynamic structure (e.g., shocks, mixing).

key_results.main_finding: No statistically significant correlation is found between the mass residual R(r) and the ICM entropy gradient |∇K(r)| in either the Bullet Cluster (ρ = −0.129, p = 0.21) or Abell 1835 (ρ = −0.052, p = 0.7), consistent with current sensitivity limits.
parameters_tested: Residual mass profile R(r) = M_lens(r) − M_HSE(r)
datasets_used: 1E 0657-56 (Bullet Cluster): JWST NIRCam lensing; Chandra (500 ks) X-ray; ACCEPT catalog profiles
Abell 1835: HST + Subaru lensing; Chandra X-ray; ACCEPT catalog profiles

sealed_predictions.statement: In a stacked sample of ≥20 clusters (n_eff ≳ 1100 radial bins) with current-quality WL+X-ray data, a true thermodynamic–lensing coupling at the ρ ≈ 0.1 level will be detectable at ≥3σ; absence of such a signal will constrain |ρ| < 0.06 at 3σ.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Stacked analysis of normalized correlations ρ(R_norm, G_norm) across ≥20 clusters combining strong+weak lensing and deprojected X-ray profiles.

sealed_predictions.statement: Any phenomenological thermodynamic–lensing coupling that is viable must preserve achromaticity of gravitational lensing and time delays to current limits.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Multi-wavelength lensing and time-delay measurements (e.g., lensed quasars) showing wavelength dependence beyond current bounds.

kill_criteria: KC1: Stacked cluster analysis with n_eff ≥ 1000 finds |ρ(R_norm, G_norm)| < 0.06 at 3σ for both merging and relaxed subsamples, ruling out percent-level thermodynamic–lensing coupling.

KC2: After accounting for non-thermal pressure, clumping, and projection with state-of-the-art HSE modeling and simulations, residuals R(r) are consistent with zero at all radii (|R|/M_lens < 3%) and show no spatial correlation with |∇K|.
KC3: Detection of wavelength-dependent lensing or time delays exceeding current achromaticity limits, indicating non-metric photon propagation incompatible with the assumed coupling class.

KC4: High-precision spectroscopic tests targeting lines-of-sight across strong ICM entropy gradients find no correlated line-of-sight redshift or asymmetry signal at instrument-limited precision, excluding proposed LOS signatures tied to |∇K|.

KC5: Independent constraints from CMB spectral distortions, BBN, and WEP tests require any additional coupling to be negligible; demonstration that a coupling large enough to explain any observed ρ would violate these bounds would kill the model class.

methodology.name: Triangulation Test
methodology.description: Compare three independent observables to test for thermodynamic-lensing coupling

observables.name: Hydrostatic Mass
observables.formula: M_HSE(<r) = -(kTr)/(μm_pG)[d ln n_e/d ln r + d ln T/d ln r]

key_caveats: Pilot results consistent with null hypothesis
No evidence for modified gravity claimed
Larger samples needed for decisive sensitivity
confounding_factors: Dynamical state coupling (shocks produce both entropy jumps and HSE deviations)
Non-thermal pressure (cosmic rays, magnetic fields, turbulence)
